title: Sell Diminishing-Valued Colored Balls
summary: You have an inventory of balls in different colors, and a customer wants to buy any number of these balls.
statement: You have an inventory of balls in different colors, and a customer wants to buy any number of these balls. The customer values each ball based on the current number of balls of that color remaining in your inventory, with the value decreasing with each sale. You are given an integer array representing the initial count of each color and an integer for the total number of balls the customer wishes to buy. Determine the maximum total value you can achieve from selling the balls, and return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Positive inventories; orders do not exceed total inventory.
Each sold ball earns its color’s current inventory, then that inventory decreases by one. Return maximum profit modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def maximum_diminishing_ball_profit(inventory, orders):
 inventory=sorted(inventory,reverse=True)+[0];answer=0;colors=1
 for index in range(len(inventory)-1):
  high,low=inventory[index],inventory[index+1];available=colors*(high-low)
  take=min(orders,available);levels,remainder=divmod(take,colors)
  answer+=colors*(high+high-levels+1)*levels//2+remainder*(high-levels);orders-=take
  if orders==0:break
  colors+=1
 return answer%1000000007

hints: Always sell a currently highest-valued ball.
Process equal-height inventory levels together using arithmetic-series sums.
Sort descending; lower the top color group toward the next height, stopping partway when orders run out.
Exchange any lower-valued sale with an available higher-valued ball to increase profit, proving descending sale order.
